tax.text: She voted against a reconciliation bill that paired tax cuts for wealthy people with cuts to Medicaid and nutrition assistance.
tax.quote: The legislation includes drastic cuts to Medicaid, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and other basic benefits, to pay for tax cuts for the wealthy and well-connected.

wages.text: Brown says she supports a $15 minimum wage indexed to inflation and backing legislation to strengthen unions.
wages.quote: I support a path to a $15 minimum wage that indexes to inflation so it has built-in increases.

trade.text: She called for repeal of President Trump's tariffs, saying they raise consumer costs.
trade.quote: We also need to repeal the President’s tariffs, which are making everything from coffee and meat to electronics and clothes more expensive.

debt.text: She helped pass legislation restoring Social Security benefits for public workers and retirees.
debt.quote: Shontel Brown helped pass the Social Security Fairness Act, which restored benefits for public workers and retirees who had been unfairly penalized.

housing.text: Brown says she will work to increase the housing supply and supports equitable zoning as part of addressing housing needs.
housing.quote: I will also work to make housing more affordable by ending discriminatory practices like redlining; provide down-payment assistance through a refundable tax credit; and will work to increase the supply of housing.

schools.text: She introduced legislation to help public schools reduce class sizes in early grades.
schools.quote: Establishes a new program to help schools reduce class sizes in K-3 grades to 18 students per class

safety.text: Brown supports crisis response options that reduce reliance on police and says she will champion the CAHOOTS Act.
safety.quote: In Cuyahoga County, I have sought to develop options so that people who call 911 have a crisis intervention option, and don’t have to rely on the police.

immigration.text: She voted for legislation extending Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and urged Senate passage.
immigration.quote: In April, I proudly voted for legislation that passed the House to extend TPS status for Haiti.

guns.text: Brown supports universal background checks, an assault weapons ban, and other restrictions on gun sales and accessories.
guns.quote: Requiring Universal Background Checks for gun sales. Every person purchasing a gun should undergo a background check.

abortion.text: Brown called for passage of the Women’s Health Protection Act to establish a nationwide right to reproductive care, including abortion.
abortion.quote: the need to pass the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would establish a nationwide right to the full range of reproductive care: abortion, contraception, family planning, miscarriage management, IVF and more.

gender.text: She voted against the House bill that would have required sex-at-birth rules for Title IX athletics.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

cannabis.text: She voted yea on House passage of the MORE Act.
cannabis.quote: Roll Call 107 | Bill Number: H. R. 3617

health.text: Brown says she supports a public option to expand coverage and would vote for Medicare for All if it came to the House floor.
health.quote: I will work with the Biden-Harris Administration to pass a high-quality public option that will lower costs, drive down prescription drug costs, and expand coverage to achieve universal health care.

energy.text: Brown supports aggressive climate action, including net-zero emissions by 2050 and a carbon-free power sector by 2035.
energy.quote: I support the principles laid out in the Green New Deal and I am committed to aggressive action on climate change with net-zero emissions by 2050 and a carbon-free power sector by 2035.

voting.text: Brown supports voting rights legislation that would expand ballot access and says voter registration should be easier.
voting.quote: We have to make it easier to register voters, and Congress should and needs to step up.

debt.text: He proposed ending future Social Security benefit accruals in 2027 and redirecting the employee OAS payroll tax to deferred tax accounts.
debt.quote: Stop the benefit accruals in 2027 and stop the 5.3% Employee FICA Tax (OAS portion) from being deposited into the OAS trust.
